title: V'Zot HaBerachah: no one knows his grave (Deuteronomy 34:5–6)
hook: God buries Moses, and no one knows his grave to this day

segments.voice: Yesterday, the view from Nebo. Your line was see it from the mountain. Today, the death of Moses, and a strange detail about his grave.

Pyramids. Mausoleums. A marble tomb with a line of visitors outside. Famous people are often given famous graves, and pilgrims travel far to stand where a founder lies, leaving flowers, candles, notes, stones. Some tombs become places of prayer. Moses, the teacher at the center of the Torah, dies on a mountain in Moab. And the text goes out of its way to tell us there is nothing to visit.
screen: `PYRAMIDS AND MAUSOLEUMS.` → `PILGRIMS AT THE TOMB.` → `NOTHING TO VISIT.`

segments.voice: So Moses, the servant of God, dies there in the land of Moab, at God's word. He is buried in a valley opposite Beth-peor, the text says, "and no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day." Who buried him? The Hebrew simply says: he buried him. Rashi says it was God, in His glory. The Talmud, in Sotah, takes that seriously and turns it into a teaching about how people should live. God clothed Adam and Eve. God visited Abraham when he was healing. God comforted Isaac when he mourned. And God buried Moses. So, the Talmud says, walk in God's ways: clothe, visit, comfort, bury. When volunteers of a chevra kadisha, a Jewish burial society, care for the body of someone who has died, they're walking in that line. And the hidden grave? The text doesn't say why. One explanation often given is that the people would have made it a place of worship, and Moses had always pointed beyond himself. Whatever the reason, the effect is clear. No shrine. No relic. What remains of Moses is what he taught. And the teaching isn't left in one place. It's in each Torah scroll, read aloud week by week. Moses' grave is unknown. His words are read wherever the scroll is opened.
screen: `MOSES DIES IN THE LAND OF MOAB.` · `WHO BURIED HIM?` · `CLOTHE, VISIT, COMFORT, BURY.` · `NO SHRINE, ONLY TEACHING.` · then, large: `NO GRAVE, ONLY TEACHING.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who has died whose words or habits still live in you, a grandmother's saying, a teacher's correction, a friend's way of laughing at trouble, and name one thing they taught you. Then think of one thing you'd like to pass on in the same way, so that it outlasts you.
V'Zot HaBerachah. And this is the blessing. A portion that ends with a death, an unknown grave, and a teaching that stays.
Your line: no grave, only teaching. His words are read wherever the scroll is opened. Day five hundred thirty-five, done.

howItsDone: Jewish tradition calls caring for the dead chesed shel emet, a true kindness, since it can't be repaid; local chevra kadisha societies prepare bodies for burial, and tradition places Moses' death on the 7th of Adar, a day some burial societies mark.

chat.meaning: And no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day: no shrine, no relic. What remains of Moses is his teaching.

chevra kadisha.meaning: a Jewish burial society of volunteers

Moab.meaning: the land east of the Jordan, where Moses dies

Beth-peor.meaning: a place in Moab; Moses is buried in a valley across from it

Sotah.meaning: a Talmud tractate: clothe, visit, comfort, bury

Rashi.meaning: a medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud

sources.quoted: and no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.

notes: Deuteronomy 34:6 final clause quoted from JPS 1917 from memory; verify. The rest of 34:5–6 is paraphrased.
Rashi on 34:6: 'He buried him: the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory'. Paraphrased.
Sotah 14a: clothe the naked (Adam and Eve), visit the sick (Abraham), comfort mourners (Isaac), bury the dead (Moses). Paraphrased.
'So the grave would not become a place of worship' is a common explanation, not stated in the text; kept as 'a common explanation'.
7 Adar as Moses' yahrzeit (Megillah 13b) is mentioned only in howItsDone; verify the chevra kadisha custom.
